Estimate totals from a Chromy sample

Source: R/estimate.R
estimate_total.Rd

The multiplicity (Hansen–Hurwitz form) estimator that matches the design: each selected unit's value divided by its effective expected hits — the ones the selection actually used — and weighted by the hits it received. For the precision there is no unbiased variance under a systematic-like design; the successive-difference estimator is the working convention, computed in list order over the units whose selection was actually random, so that it reads the local variation the ordering left behind. Units selected with certainty contribute no variance.

Usage

estimate_total(sample, variables)

Arguments

sample

A chromy_sample().

variables

Names of the study columns to estimate, numeric columns of the sampled frame.

Value

A tibble with one row per variable: variable, total, se (the successive-difference standard error; NA when only one hit was random), cv_pct, and random_draws, the number of units the variance is computed over.

Examples

set.seed(7)
frame <- data.frame(size = rlnorm(80, 3), y = rlnorm(80, 5))
s <- chromy_sample(frame, n = 25, size = "size")
estimate_total(s, "y")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   variable  total    se cv_pct random_draws
#>   <chr>     <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 y        23879. 6865.   28.8           18
